title: Adult Learning Principles for GIS Instruction: Lessons Learned from a Teaching Wildland Fire Professionals
presenter: Heather Heward (Forest, Rangeland and Fire Sciences, University of Idaho)
description_full:
You may be a GIS wizard in map production, sharing, and collaboration, but how do you handle a classroom of students facing countless error messages from self-inflicted or program-related issues, or even a lab mate who sucks up your work time with their GIS problems? Your ability to share your knowledge about GIS while fostering a growth mindset for the people you work with is the real mark of a GIS master. Hear my lessons learned from decades of teaching wildland fire professional GIS, and have an interactive discussion on how to use adult learning principles to maximize your effectiveness as a teacher of GIS and prepare the next generation of GIS teachers.

##### Bio 

Heather Heward is director of the Student of Fire Initiative and a Research Assistant Professor in Forest, Rangeland, and Fire Sciences who investigates wildland fire behavior and training design. Her recent work examines how federal prescribed fire training can be improved using adult learning principles. She has also studied the relationship between fire intensity and burn severity using satellite remote sensing data from western U.S. fires.

title: Better Understanding Wildfire with Spatial Data: Pre-fire, Post-fire, and Past-fires
presenter: Keith T. Weber (GIS Director, Idaho State University)
description_full:
This presentation will discuss how spatial data and GIS can be used to model fire susceptibility, hazard, risk, and conflagration risk using GIS and satellite remote sensing capabilities. The resulting models can be used to inform decision-makers and enable science-driven pre-fire mitigation planning. We will also look at the RECOVER post-fire decision support platform and its ability to help manage and monitor the post-fire landscape. Lastly, we will dive into the Historic Fires Database to better understand the broader wildfire landscape and burn-on-burn events.

title: Remotely Sensed Data in Natural Resources
presenter: Jason Karl (Director of the Rangeland Center, Rangeland Ecology, University of Idaho); Ed Flathers (College of Natural Resources Forest Innovations Institute, University of Idaho); Bruce Ripley (Chief innovation officer, College of Natural Resources, University of Idaho)
description_full:
Remote sensed data in natural resource comes in many forms. This session will focus on how some of the more advanced remote sensing techniques such as gaussian splatting are transforming data collection, how those images are transformed into not just an immersive 3D environment but a complete high resolution 3D dataset that can be geolocated with other GIS information to make a complete high resolution digital twin of your study area.

Individual talks:

- Dr. Jason Karl - Collection of high resolution imagery and transformation into a gaussian splat.
- Dr. Ed Flathers - High precision georeferencing of unregistered drone information, co-registering those data with high precision LiDAR point clouds and transformation into a single product.
- Bruce Ripley - How we put high resolution remote sensed data to use in the applied world to make decisions and how a digital forest twin is much more than a collection of trees.
